findings.text: A per-CPU capability query examines one numbered feature bit inside the capability vector carried by a supplied CPU information record and reports presence as boolean.
A current-CPU query first applies a compile-time required-mask shortcut that forces true for mandatory bits, otherwise it tests the named bit in the current CPU capability area.
Setting a capability marks the requested bit position inside the target CPU record capability vector and setting a bug uses the same marking operation.

A static boot-CPU optimized query chooses at compile time between a constant-folded boot-CPU result and a runtime patched branch that inspects the boot capability byte for the requested bit and returns true or false.

Hardware bug status reuses the capability mechanism: bug lookup aliases capability lookup, bug setting aliases capability setting, boot-CPU bug lookup and setting operate on boot data, forced bug setup aliases forced capability setup, and a separate bug flag array is indexed by bug number.
A generic feature-presence name is an alias for the boot-CPU capability query, so callers checking global availability observe boot CPU state.
Capability storage sizing is twenty-two 32-bit words for features and two 32-bit words for bugs, with total feature count defined as feature words multiplied by thirty-two.
Every feature identifier encodes a word index multiplied by thirty-two plus a bit offset within that word, spanning words zero through eight in these fragments.

Word zero holds legacy baseline integer and floating and memory features, word one holds extended syscall NX large-page and 64-bit indicators, word three holds timer topology perfmon and TSC reliability indicators, word four holds virtualization SIMD crypto and random indicators, word five holds vendor crypto and RNG enable pairs, word six holds AMD virtualization and perf extensions, word seven holds mitigation isolation and cache allocation controls, word eight holds hypervisor and confidential guest indicators.
CPU identity for feature reporting is conveyed as vendor plus family plus model numeric fields taken from boot CPU data and rendered as fixed-width hexadecimal fields in one type label.
Fragments imply a CPU record containing a capability vector addressable both as words and as bytes, plus vendor family and model scalar fields used for identification.

Boot-CPU and current-CPU queries are not interchangeable: static and boot helpers inspect global boot data while per-CPU and current-CPU helpers inspect a specific record, so use of the boot variant on heterogeneous systems can misreport local availability.
